Bases : Reader

This class controls the radiative transfer component of the forward model. An ordered dictionary is maintained of individual RTMs (MODTRAN, for example). We loop over the dictionary concatenating the radiation and derivatives from each RTM and interval to form the complete result.

In general, some of the state vector components will be shared between RTMs and bands. For example, H20STR is shared between both VISNIR and TIR. This class maintains the master list of statevectors.

source staticmethod BaseAtmosphere.two_albedo_method(case_0: dict, case_1: dict, case_2: dict, coszen: float, rfl_1: float = 0.1, rfl_2: float = 0.5) → dict

Calculates split transmittance values from a multipart file using the two-albedo method. See notes for further detail.

Parameters

  • case_0 : dict — MODTRAN output for a non-reflective surface (case 0 of the channel file)

  • case_1 : dict — MODTRAN output for surface reflectance = rfl_1 (case 1 of the channel file)

  • case_2 : dict — MODTRAN output for surface reflectance = rfl_2 (case 2 of the channel file)

  • coszen : float — cosine of the solar zenith angle

  • rfl_1 : float, defaults=0.1 — surface reflectance for case 1 of the MODTRAN output

  • rfl_2 : float, defaults=0.5 — surface reflectance for case 2 of the MODTRAN output

Returns

  • data : dict — Relevant information

Notes

This implementation follows Guanter et al. (2009) (DOI:10.1080/01431160802438555), modified by Nimrod Carmon. It is called the "2-albedo" method, referring to running MODTRAN with 2 different surface albedos. Alternatively, one could also run the 3-albedo method, which is similar to this one with the single difference where the "path_radiance_no_surface" variable is taken from a zero-surface-reflectance MODTRAN run instead of being calculated from 2 MODTRAN outputs.

There are a few argument as to why the 2- or 3-albedo methods are beneficial: (1) For each grid point on the lookup table you sample MODTRAN 2 or 3 times, i.e., you get 2 or 3 "data points" for the atmospheric parameter of interest. This in theory allows us to use a lower band model resolution for the MODTRAN run, which is much faster, while keeping high accuracy. (2) We use the decoupled transmittance products to expand the forward model and account for more physics, currently topography and glint.

source class SerialEncoder(*, skipkeys=False, ensure_ascii=True, check_circular=True, allow_nan=True, sort_keys=False, indent=None, separators=None, default=None)

Bases : json.JSONEncoder

Encoder for json to help ensure json objects can be passed to the workflow manager.

Constructor for JSONEncoder, with sensible defaults.

If skipkeys is false, then it is a TypeError to attempt encoding of keys that are not str, int, float, bool or None. If skipkeys is True, such items are simply skipped.

If ensure_ascii is true, the output is guaranteed to be str objects with all incoming non-ASCII characters escaped. If ensure_ascii is false, the output can contain non-ASCII characters.

If check_circular is true, then lists, dicts, and custom encoded objects will be checked for circular references during encoding to prevent an infinite recursion (which would cause an RecursionError). Otherwise, no such check takes place.

If allow_nan is true, then NaN, Infinity, and -Infinity will be encoded as such. This behavior is not JSON specification compliant, but is consistent with most JavaScript based encoders and decoders. Otherwise, it will be a ValueError to encode such floats.

If sort_keys is true, then the output of dictionaries will be sorted by key; this is useful for regression tests to ensure that JSON serializations can be compared on a day-to-day basis.

If indent is a non-negative integer, then JSON array elements and object members will be pretty-printed with that indent level. An indent level of 0 will only insert newlines. None is the most compact representation.

If specified, separators should be an (item_separator, key_separator) tuple. The default is (', ', ': ') if indent is None and (',', ': ') otherwise. To get the most compact JSON representation, you should specify (',', ':') to eliminate whitespace.

If specified, default is a function that gets called for objects that can't otherwise be serialized. It should return a JSON encodable version of the object or raise a TypeError.

source method SRTMnetModel.predict(surrogate_data, surrogate_data_emulator_wl, batch_size=4096, response_scaler=None, response_offset=None, resample_dict=None)

Predicts model output for either 6c or 3c model. General model formulation is

x = surrogate_data y = emulator(x) / response_scaler + response_offset + x return < y > resampled to desired wavelengths

In the case of the 6c model, we also calculate all coupled terms at high spectral resolution, converting to radiance and then convolving. We leave transmitance and sphalb in 'transmittance units', but convert rhoatm to radiance.

In contrast, the 3c model convolves directly in transmittance units. This is undesireable, but we have left for historical consistency. Ideally, user will shift to the 6c model.

Parameters

  • surrogate_data — input data as numpy or dask array

  • surrogate_data_emulator_wl — input data at emulator wavelengths (interpolated surrogate)

  • batch_size : int, optional — Size of batch to process. Defaults to 4096.

  • response_scaler : list, optional — list of scalers for each output component. Defaults to None.

  • response_offset : list, optional — list of offsets for each output component. Defaults to None

  • resample_dict : dict, optional — dictionary containing resampling parameters. Defaults to None.

Returns

  • np.array — emulated output

This class controls the radiative transfer component of the forward model. An ordered dictionary is maintained of individual RTMs (MODTRAN, for example). We loop over the dictionary concatenating the radiation and derivatives from each RTM and interval to form the complete result.

In general, some of the state vector components will be shared between RTMs and bands. For example, H20STR is shared between both VISNIR and TIR. This class maintains the master list of statevectors.

source staticmethod BaseAtmosphere.two_albedo_method(case_0: dict, case_1: dict, case_2: dict, coszen: float, rfl_1: float = 0.1, rfl_2: float = 0.5) → dict

Calculates split transmittance values from a multipart file using the two-albedo method. See notes for further detail.

Parameters

  • case_0 : dict — MODTRAN output for a non-reflective surface (case 0 of the channel file)

  • case_1 : dict — MODTRAN output for surface reflectance = rfl_1 (case 1 of the channel file)

  • case_2 : dict — MODTRAN output for surface reflectance = rfl_2 (case 2 of the channel file)

  • coszen : float — cosine of the solar zenith angle

  • rfl_1 : float, defaults=0.1 — surface reflectance for case 1 of the MODTRAN output

  • rfl_2 : float, defaults=0.5 — surface reflectance for case 2 of the MODTRAN output

Returns

  • data : dict — Relevant information

Notes

This implementation follows Guanter et al. (2009) (DOI:10.1080/01431160802438555), modified by Nimrod Carmon. It is called the "2-albedo" method, referring to running MODTRAN with 2 different surface albedos. Alternatively, one could also run the 3-albedo method, which is similar to this one with the single difference where the "path_radiance_no_surface" variable is taken from a zero-surface-reflectance MODTRAN run instead of being calculated from 2 MODTRAN outputs.

There are a few argument as to why the 2- or 3-albedo methods are beneficial: (1) For each grid point on the lookup table you sample MODTRAN 2 or 3 times, i.e., you get 2 or 3 "data points" for the atmospheric parameter of interest. This in theory allows us to use a lower band model resolution for the MODTRAN run, which is much faster, while keeping high accuracy. (2) We use the decoupled transmittance products to expand the forward model and account for more physics, currently topography and glint.

source class Config(**data: Any)

Bases : SectionModel

Main ISOFIT configuration model.

This Pydantic model validates and manages all ISOFIT configuration parameters, including input/output files, forward model components (surface, atmosphere, instrument), and implementation settings.

Create a new model by parsing and validating input data from keyword arguments.

Raises [ValidationError][pydantic_core.ValidationError] if the input data cannot be validated to form a valid model.

self is explicitly positional-only to allow self as a field name.

Examples

With no arguments, the Config is built from the default base config:

from isofit.configs import Config
config = Config()
config.forward_model.atmosphere.engine.name

'prebuilt'

Start from an alternative base config with base; the remaining keywords are deep-merged on top (see :class:~isofit.configs.base.SectionModel):

config = Config(
    base="vswir",
    forward_model={"surface": {"surface_file": "surface.mat"}},
    implementation={"n_cores": 4},
)
config.forward_model.atmosphere.engine.name

'srtmnet'

config.get_config_errors()  # Validate inter-field constraints

Attributes

  • model_config : ClassVar[ConfigDict] — Configuration for the model, should be a dictionary conforming to [ConfigDict][pydantic.config.ConfigDict].

  • model_extra : Dict[str, Any] | None — Get extra fields set during validation.

  • model_fields_set : set[str] — Returns the set of fields that have been explicitly set on this model instance.

  • defaults : ClassVar[str] — Base config used when base is not given. Engine sections override this with their own base (e.g. "sixs"), since default only defines the prebuilt engine.

Methods

  • get_config_errors — Check configuration validity and raise errors if found.

source method Config.get_config_errors() → None

Check configuration validity and raise errors if found.

This method provides backward compatibility with the legacy Config.get_config_errors() method. With Pydantic, most validation happens at construction time, so this method primarily performs additional inter-field validation checks that span multiple sections.

Parameters

  • None

Returns

  • None — None

Raises

  • AttributeError — If configuration errors are found during inter-field validation. All errors are logged before raising.

Examples 

from isofit.configs import Config
config = Config(
    base="vswir",
    forward_model={"surface": {"surface_file": "surface.mat"}},
)
config.get_config_errors()  # No errors
config.implementation.mode = "simulation"  # Without a reflectance_file
config.get_config_errors()

Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
AttributeError: Configuration error(s) found. See log for details.

Notes

The following inter-field validations are performed: - Simulation mode requires input.reflectance_file to be set - The surface checks of :meth:SurfaceConfig.get_config_issues, which read the surface model files

source create_new_config(file: Union[str, Path], **kwargs) → Config

Load a config and validate it into a :class:~isofit.configs.Config.

Legacy loading function, to be deprecated in the config refactor part 2.

When file is a path, relative paths in the config (values of keys containing file, directory, or path) are expanded against the config file's directory, not the current working directory. Values that are ${...} references are left for interpolation.

Parameters

  • file : str or pathlib.Path — Path to a config file or the name of a base config; see :func:load.

  • **kwargs — Passed through to :func:load (section, overrides, interp).

Returns

  • Config — The validated config.

Raises

  • ValueError — If file is neither an existing file nor a known base config.

  • pydantic.ValidationError — If the loaded config fails validation.

Examples 

from isofit.configs import create_new_config
config = create_new_config("config.yaml")

source class AtmosphereConfig(**data: Any)

Bases : SectionModel

Atmosphere configuration.

Configures atmospheric radiative transfer modeling including RT engine (MODTRAN, 6S, LibRadTran, sRTMnet, or prebuilt), lookup table generation and storage, and atmospheric state vector parameters.

Create a new model by parsing and validating input data from keyword arguments.

Raises [ValidationError][pydantic_core.ValidationError] if the input data cannot be validated to form a valid model.

self is explicitly positional-only to allow self as a field name.

Examples

The default base config uses a prebuilt LUT with an empty grid:

from isofit.configs.sections.atmosphere import AtmosphereConfig
atm = AtmosphereConfig()
atm.engine.name, atm.lut_grid

('prebuilt', {})

The vswir base config uses sRTMnet and retrieves water vapor and aerosol:

atm = AtmosphereConfig(base="vswir")
atm.engine.name, list(atm.lut_grid)

('srtmnet', ['AOT550', 'H2OSTR'])

Each engine profile seeds its own engine defaults:

atm = AtmosphereConfig(
    base="sixs",
    lut_grid={
        "H2OSTR": [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5],
        "AOT550": [0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3],
    },
    statevector_names=["H2OSTR", "AOT550"],
)
atm.engine.name, atm.statevector_names

('sixs', ['AOT550', 'H2OSTR'])

source package isofit.configs.sections.atmosphere.engines

Atmospheric radiative transfer engine configurations.

This module provides Pydantic models for various RT engines supported by ISOFIT, including MODTRAN, 6S, LibRadTran, sRTMnet, and prebuilt LUTs. It uses discriminated unions to handle different engine types with a common interface.

Classes

  • ModtranConfig — MODTRAN 6.0 engine configuration.

  • sRTMnetConfig — sRTMnet engine configuration.

Functions

  • standardName — Standardize engine names to canonical form.

  • selectByName — Discriminator function to select the config model for a given engine name.

source standardName(name: str) → str

Standardize engine names to canonical form.

Enables multiple name aliases for each engine and normalizes them to a standard name used internally in the codebase. If the only acceptable name for an engine is its lowercased form, it does not need special handling.

Parameters

  • name : str — Engine name to standardize (case-insensitive).

Returns

  • str — Standardized engine name.

Examples 

standardName("6S")

'sixs'

standardName("SIXS")

'sixs'

standardName("kf")

'kernelflows'

standardName("MODTRAN")

'modtran'

Notes

Supported aliases: - "6s", "sixs" -> "sixs" - "kf", "kernelflows" -> "kernelflows" - All other names are lowercased

source selectByName(data: dict) → str

Discriminator function to select the config model for a given engine name.

Used by Pydantic's discriminated union to route configuration dictionaries to the correct engine model class based on the 'name' field.

Parameters

  • data : dict — Configuration dictionary containing 'name' field.

Returns

  • str — Standardized engine name for discriminator matching.

Notes

This function is called automatically by Pydantic during validation and should not be invoked directly by users.

source module isofit.configs.sections.atmosphere.statevector

Atmosphere state vector and unknowns configuration models.

Unlike the surface and instrument state vectors, whose elements are a fixed set of named fields, the atmospheric state vector is populated dynamically from the LUT grid (H2OSTR, CO2, AOT550, surface_elevation_km, AERFRAC_*, ...). These models are therefore modeled as typed mappings (:class:pydantic.RootModel over a dict), which validates each entry automatically, while still exposing the historical get_elements/get_element_names accessor API the runtime relies on.

Classes

  • AtmosphereStateVectorConfig — Atmospheric state vector with dynamic, LUT-driven element names.

  • AtmosphereUnknownsConfig — Radiative-transfer unknowns (unmodeled-variable uncertainties).

source class AtmosphereStateVectorConfig()

Bases : StateVectorValueMixin, RootModel[dict[str, StateVectorElementConfig]]

Atmospheric state vector with dynamic, LUT-driven element names.

Elements are supplied as a mapping of arbitrary keys (one per retrieved atmospheric parameter) to :class:StateVectorElementConfig values. Pydantic validates (and coerces plain dicts into) the element configs automatically. The accessor methods iterate over these dynamic entries rather than a fixed set of declared fields.

Examples 

from isofit.configs.sections.atmosphere.statevector import (
    AtmosphereStateVectorConfig,
)
sv = AtmosphereStateVectorConfig(
    {"H2OSTR": {"bounds": [0.5, 2.5], "init": 1.5}}
)
sv.get_element_names()

['H2OSTR']

Methods

  • get_elements — Return (elements, names) for all dynamic elements, sorted by name.

  • get_element_names — Return the names of all dynamic elements, sorted.

  • get_all_element_names — Return the names of every dynamic element, in insertion order.

  • get_all_elements — Return the value of every dynamic element, in insertion order.

  • get — Return the element with the given name, or [] if not set.

source method SurfaceConfig.update_from_subconfig(subconfig: SubSurfaceConfig)

Overwrite fields from a per-class multi-surface sub-config.

In multi-surface mode each surface class carries its own settings; this copies them onto the active SurfaceConfig. Structural fields that describe the multi-surface machinery itself (or the state vector) are never overwritten, and unknown keys are ignored.

Parameters

  • subconfig : SubSurfaceConfig — Settings for the selected surface class.

source method SurfaceConfig.get_config_issues() → tuple[list[str], list[str]]

Check the config for completeness and against the surface model files.

These checks run from :meth:isofit.configs.Config.get_config_errors rather than at validation time: base configs (e.g. default.yml) intentionally leave the surface file unset, and the surface model files may not have been built yet when the config is loaded.

Returns

  • tuple[list[str], list[str]] — Errors and warnings found.

Notes

Checks performed: - Outside multi-surface mode, surface_file and surface_category must be set - Statevector elements (e.g. SURF_TEMP_K) configured for each surface file should match those stored in it; a mismatch is a warning, as the configured values are used. The base statevector applies to every file, and a sub-surface's own statevector overrides it for that sub-surface's file. Files that don't exist yet are skipped

source package isofit.configs.utils.interpolate

Configuration interpolation utilities for variable substitution.

This package loads configuration files with inheritance, override, and variable interpolation support. It allows using ${key} or ${.key} syntax to reference other values within the configuration, and supports command-line overrides through Click contexts.

Configs are plain nested dict / list trees throughout.

The pipeline, run in order by :func:load, is split into one module per stage:

  • :mod:.common -- :func:read plus the dict helpers :func:get_dotted, :func:locate, :func:set_dotted, and :func:merge
  • :mod:.inherit -- ^^ inheritance (:func:patch, :func:resolve_file)
  • :mod:.overrides -- dotted-key overrides (:func:parse_overrides, :func:override)
  • :mod:.resolve -- ${...} interpolation (:func:interp, :func:interpolate)
  • :mod:.load -- :func:load, which chains the stages above
  • :mod:.cli -- the isofit config command group

Functions

  • get_dotted — Look up a value in a nested dict/list tree by dotted key.

  • locate — Find where a dotted key lives in a nested dict/list tree.

  • merge — Deep-merge src into dst in place; src wins on conflict.

  • read — Load a config file into a dict, dispatching on its extension.

  • set_dotted — Set a value in a nested dict/list tree by dotted key, in place.

  • patch — Merge one or more referenced sections into box in place.

  • resolve_file — Resolve a cross-file ^^ reference of the form path[:section].

  • load — Loads a config from a yaml or json file

  • override — Patch the config in place with dotted key/value overrides.

  • parse_overrides — Normalize any override specification into a plain {dotted.key: value} dict.

  • interp — Interpolate ${...} references in a single string against the config.

  • interpolate — Recursively interpolate every ${...} reference in a config tree in place.

source get_dotted(data: Union[dict, list], key: str) → Any

Look up a value in a nested dict/list tree by dotted key.

Mapping keys are separated by . and list items are indexed with [i], so "a.b[1].c" is data["a"]["b"][1]["c"]. Negative indices count from the end.

A literal key always wins over descending, and each separator is tried as a split point from left to right. This lets a key that itself contains dots be addressed: with {"env": {"srtmnet": "/p", "srtmnet.file": "f.h5"}}, "env.srtmnet.file" resolves to "f.h5".

Parameters

  • data : dict or list — The tree to search.

  • key : str — Dotted key, e.g. "forward_model.instrument.SNR" or "implementation.inversion.windows[0]". An empty key returns data itself.

Returns

  • Any — The value at key.

Raises

  • KeyError — If key does not resolve to a value, including when it indexes past the end of a list or descends into a scalar.

Examples 

data = {"a": {"b": [{"c": 1}, {"c": 2}]}}
get_dotted(data, "a.b[1].c")

2

get_dotted(data, "a.b[-1]")

{'c': 2}

source locate(data: Union[dict, list], key: str) → list[tuple[Union[dict, list], Any]]

Find where a dotted key lives in a nested dict/list tree.

Resolves key exactly as :func:get_dotted does, but returns the path taken rather than the value, so callers can tell which section a value belongs to and update it in place.

Parameters

  • data : dict or list — The tree to search.

  • key : str — Dotted key, e.g. "a.b[1].c".

Returns

  • list of (dict or list, str or int) — Each (container, slot) step from data down to the value, which is path[-1][0][path[-1][1]]. List indices are normalised to be non-negative. An empty key returns an empty path.

Raises

  • KeyError — If key does not resolve to a value.

Examples 

data = {"a": {"b": [{"c": 1}, {"c": 2}]}}
[slot for _, slot in locate(data, "a.b[-1].c")]

['a', 'b', 1, 'c']

source merge(dst: dict, src: dict) → dict

Deep-merge src into dst in place; src wins on conflict.

Nested mappings are merged key by key. Every other value, including lists and an explicit None, replaces the value in dst outright. Values taken from src are deep-copied, so later mutation of dst never reaches back into src.

Parameters

  • dst : dict — The mapping to update.

  • src : dict — The mapping to merge on top.

Returns

  • dict — The same dst, updated.

source read(config: Union[str, Path]) → dict

Load a config file into a dict, dispatching on its extension.

Both YAML (.yml / .yaml) and JSON (.json) are supported. An empty file loads as an empty dict.

Parameters

  • config : str or pathlib.Path — File path to the config to read.

Returns

  • dict — The loaded configuration.

Raises

  • ValueError — If the file's extension is not a supported config format, or the file's top level is not a mapping.

source set_dotted(data: Union[dict, list], key: str, value: Any) → None

Set a value in a nested dict/list tree by dotted key, in place.

Uses the same key resolution as :func:get_dotted, including [i] list indexing. Missing or null intermediate sections are created as empty dicts. Lists are never created or extended, so an indexed item must already exist.

A mapping assigned onto an existing mapping is deep-merged into it (see :func:merge), so other keys of that section are kept. Any other value, including lists and None, replaces the existing one outright. The value is deep-copied, so data never aliases it.

Parameters

  • data : dict or list — The tree to update.

  • key : str — Dotted key, e.g. "forward_model.instrument.SNR" or "implementation.inversion.windows[0]".

  • value : Any — Value to assign.

Raises

  • KeyError — If a list index in key is malformed or out of range.

  • TypeError — If an intermediate section of key is not the container the key expects: a mapping before ., a list before [i].

Examples 

data = {"a": {"b": [1, 2], "c": {"x": 1}}, "n": None}
set_dotted(data, "a.b[-1]", 3)
set_dotted(data, "a.c", {"y": 2})
set_dotted(data, "n.k", 4)
data

{'a': {'b': [1, 3], 'c': {'x': 1, 'y': 2}}, 'n': {'k': 4}}

source patch(box: dict, full: dict, _seen: Optional[set] = None, base_dir: Optional[Path] = None, cache: Optional[dict] = None, file: Optional[Path] = None) → dict

Merge one or more referenced sections into box in place.

Consumes the ^^ key from box, whose value names either a single section (str) or several sections (list). Each name is treated as an inherited default; they are applied lowest-priority first, in the order listed, and box's own keys always win on conflict. Referenced sections are resolved recursively, so a section that itself declares ^^ has its own ancestors folded in first.

For example A: {^^: [B, C]} with B: {^^: D} yields the precedence D < B < C < A (A's own keys highest, D lowest).

References may point either at a section in the same file (^^: default) or at a section in another file using file:section syntax (^^: bases/default.yml:srtmnet). The referenced file may be YAML or JSON. The file portion is resolved relative to base_dir (the directory of the file being loaded); a bare file with no :section inherits that file's top-level mapping.

Parameters

  • box : dict — The config subsection to patch; mutated in place. Its ^^ key is removed.

  • full : dict — The full config used to resolve same-file section names.

  • _seen : set, optional — Internal set of (file, section) keys currently being resolved on this recursion chain, used to detect circular ^^ references. Should not be passed by callers.

  • base_dir : pathlib.Path, optional — Directory used to resolve the file portion of cross-file references. Defaults to the current working directory.

  • cache : dict, optional — Internal mapping of resolved file path to its loaded config, so each referenced file is read from disk only once per patch tree.

  • file : pathlib.Path, optional — Resolved path of the file full was read from. Same-file references are identified by it for cycle detection, so sections that share a name across files are not mistaken for one another. Defaults to None, which treats full as an anonymous in-memory config.

Returns

  • dict — The same box, updated with the merged sections.

Raises

  • ValueError

  • KeyError

source resolve_file(sect: str, base_dir: Path, cache: dict) → tuple

Resolve a cross-file ^^ reference of the form path[:section].

The path is taken relative to base_dir (the directory of the file that declared the reference) and loaded at most once per patch tree via cache. With no :section suffix the referenced file's top-level mapping is inherited; otherwise the named section within it is used.

The split is made on the colon that immediately follows a supported file extension (.yml / .yaml / .json), so colons elsewhere in the path are left untouched.

Parameters

  • sect : str — The raw reference string, e.g. bases/default.yml:srtmnet or ../common.json.

  • base_dir : pathlib.Path — Directory used to resolve path relative references.

  • cache : dict — Mapping of resolved file path to loaded config, mutated in place.

Returns

  • tuple — (ref_full, ref, ref_dir, ident) where ref_full is the referenced file's full config (for resolving that file's own same-file ^^ refs), ref is a copy of the selected subsection, ref_dir is the directory of the referenced file (base for its cross-file refs), and ident is a hashable (path, section) identity for cycle detection.

Raises

  • FileNotFoundError

  • KeyError

source load(config: str, section: Optional[str] = None, ctx: Optional[click.Context] = None, interp: bool = True) → dict

Loads a config from a yaml or json file

Parameters

  • config : str — File path to the config (.yml, .yaml, or .json)

  • section : str — Returns only this subsection of the config

  • ctx : click.Context or list of str or dict, default=None — Overrides, in any shape accepted by :func:~.overrides.parse_overrides

  • interp : bool, default=True — Calls interpolate on the config before returning

Returns

  • config : dict — Loaded configuration

Raises

  • KeyError — If section is not a top-level section of the file.

source override(box: dict, ctx: Union[click.Context, list[str], dict, None]) → dict

Patch the config in place with dotted key/value overrides.

The overrides may be given in any shape accepted by :func:parse_overrides (click.Context, CLI arg list, or dict); normalization is delegated there, so this function only applies an already-canonical mapping. Keys are dotted (see :func:~.common.set_dotted), so "forward_model.instrument.SNR" resolves into nested sections, creating any that are missing.

A mapping overriding an existing section is deep-merged into it, keeping the section's other keys; any other value, including lists and None, replaces the existing one outright.

Parameters

  • box : dict — The loaded config to override; mutated in place.

  • ctx : click.Context or list of str or dict or None — The overrides, in any shape accepted by :func:parse_overrides.

Returns

  • dict — The same box, updated with the overrides.

source parse_overrides(source: Union[click.Context, list[str], dict, None]) → dict

Normalize any override specification into a plain {dotted.key: value} dict.

This is the single place that knows the different shapes overrides can arrive in, so the rest of the code only ever deals with a dict:

  • None -> {} (no overrides);
  • a click.Context -> its extra --dotted.key value args are parsed;
  • a list[str] of those same CLI tokens -> parsed directly;
  • a dict of dotted keys to already-typed values -> returned as-is.

Only the CLI forms are literal-parsed; mapping values are used verbatim, so callers passing a dict provide real Python objects (SNR=500, not "500").

Parameters

  • source : click.Context or list of str or dict or None — The override specification in any supported shape.

Returns

  • dict — Mapping of dotted key (e.g. "forward_model.instrument.SNR") to value.

source interp(val: str, rel: dict, full: dict, _seen: Optional[set] = None) → Any

Interpolate ${...} references in a single string against the config.

Format: ${.key} or ${key}. A leading dot makes the key relative to the subsection the original value lives in (rel); otherwise it resolves from the top of the config (full). After substitution the result is parsed as a Python literal when possible, so a fully-substituted string can become e.g. an int/list.

Referenced values are resolved depth-first in their own context before being substituted: a referenced string has its relative refs resolved against its own section, and a referenced list or mapping is fully interpolated. Either way the resolved value is written back into the config, so each value is resolved once and the result does not depend on key order.

Parameters

  • val : str — The value to interpolate.

  • rel : dict — The subsection used to resolve relative (${.key}) references.

  • full : dict — The full config used to resolve absolute (${key}) references.

  • _seen : set, optional — Internal set of the values currently being resolved on this recursion chain, used to detect circular references. Should not be passed by callers.

Returns

  • Any — The interpolated value; a literal (int/list/...) when it parses as one, otherwise the substituted string (or val unchanged if it had no refs).

Raises

  • ValueError

  • KeyError

source interpolate(box: Union[dict, list], full: Optional[dict] = None, rel: Optional[dict] = None, _seen: Optional[set] = None) → Union[dict, list]

Recursively interpolate every ${...} reference in a config tree in place.

Walks box (a dict or list), replacing each string value via :func:interp. full is the full config used for absolute references; rel is the current subsection used for relative ones. Both default to box itself on the first call and are threaded down as the walk descends into subsections.

:func:interp resolves each referenced value depth-first and writes it back, so the result is the same whatever order the keys are walked in.

Parameters

  • box : dict or list — The config node to interpolate; mutated in place.

  • full : dict, optional — Full config for absolute references. Defaults to box on the first call.

  • rel : dict, optional — Subsection for relative references. Defaults to full.

  • _seen : set, optional — Internal set of the values currently being resolved, used by :func:interp to detect circular references. Should not be passed by callers.

Returns

  • dict or list — The same box, with all ${...} references interpolated.

source module isofit.configs.utils.interpolate.common

Shared file reading and nested-dict helpers for the config interpolation pipeline.

This is the leaf module of the package: every other stage imports from here, and it imports from none of them.

Configs are plain nested dict / list trees. Nested values are addressed with dotted keys ("forward_model.instrument.SNR"), with [i] for list items ("implementation.inversion.windows[0]"), through :func:get_dotted and :func:set_dotted, and sections are layered with :func:merge.

Functions

  • read — Load a config file into a dict, dispatching on its extension.

  • split_points — Yield every way to split key into a head and the rest, left to right.

  • split_index — Split a leading [i] off key, checking i is in range of data.

  • get_dotted — Look up a value in a nested dict/list tree by dotted key.

  • locate — Find where a dotted key lives in a nested dict/list tree.

  • set_dotted — Set a value in a nested dict/list tree by dotted key, in place.

  • assign — Set parent[slot] to a copy of value, deep-merging when both it and the existing value are mappings.

  • set_within — Set rest within parent[slot], creating a mapping there if it is missing or None and rest names a mapping key.

  • merge — Deep-merge src into dst in place; src wins on conflict.

source read(config: Union[str, Path]) → dict

Load a config file into a dict, dispatching on its extension.

Both YAML (.yml / .yaml) and JSON (.json) are supported. An empty file loads as an empty dict.

Parameters

Returns

Raises

source split_points(key: str) → Iterator[tuple[str, str, type]]

Yield every way to split key into a head and the rest, left to right.

A . separates two mapping keys and is dropped. A [ starts a list index and is kept on the rest.

Parameters

Yields

  • head : str — The key before the split point.

  • rest : str — The key after the split point.

source split_index(data: list, key: str) → tuple[int, str]

Split a leading [i] off key, checking i is in range of data.

Parameters

  • key : str — Key starting with a list index, e.g. "[0].name".

Returns

  • rest : str — The remainder of the key, with any leading . dropped.

Raises

Mapping keys are separated by . and list items are indexed with [i], so "a.b[1].c" is data["a"]["b"][1]["c"]. Negative indices count from the end.

source locate(data: Union[dict, list], key: str) → list[tuple[Union[dict, list], Any]]

Find where a dotted key lives in a nested dict/list tree.

source module isofit.configs.utils.interpolate.inherit

Stage 1 of the pipeline: inheritance via the ^^ key.

A section declaring ^^: <ref> has the referenced section(s) merged in underneath it. References may be same-file (^^: default) or cross-file (^^: bases/default.yml:srtmnet).

Functions

source patch(box: dict, full: dict, _seen: Optional[set] = None, base_dir: Optional[Path] = None, cache: Optional[dict] = None, file: Optional[Path] = None) → dict

Merge one or more referenced sections into box in place.

Consumes the ^^ key from box, whose value names either a single section (str) or several sections (list). Each name is treated as an inherited default; they are applied lowest-priority first, in the order listed, and box's own keys always win on conflict. Referenced sections are resolved recursively, so a section that itself declares ^^ has its own ancestors folded in first.

References may point either at a section in the same file (^^: default) or at a section in another file using file:section syntax (^^: bases/default.yml:srtmnet). The referenced file may be YAML or JSON.   • full : dict — The full config used to resolve same-file section names.

  • _seen : set, optional — Internal set of (file, section) keys currently being resolved on this recursion chain, used to detect circular ^^ references. Should not be passed by callers.

source resolve_file(sect: str, base_dir: Path, cache: dict) → tuple

Resolve a cross-file ^^ reference of the form path[:section].

The path is taken relative to base_dir (the directory of the file that declared the reference) and loaded at most once per patch tree via cache. With no :section suffix the referenced file's top-level mapping is inherited; otherwise the named section within it is used.

The split is made on the colon that immediately follows a supported file extension (.yml / .yaml / .json), so colons elsewhere in the path are left untouched.

Parameters

  • sect : str — The raw reference string, e.g. bases/default.yml:srtmnet or ../common.json.

  • base_dir : pathlib.Path — Directory used to resolve path relative references.

  • cache : dict — Mapping of resolved file path to loaded config, mutated in place.

Returns

  • tuple — (ref_full, ref, ref_dir, ident) where ref_full is the referenced file's full config (for resolving that file's own same-file ^^ refs), ref is a copy of the selected subsection, ref_dir is the directory of the referenced file (base for its cross-file refs), and ident is a hashable (path, section) identity for cycle detection.

Raises

  • FileNotFoundError

  • KeyError

source module isofit.configs.utils.interpolate.overrides

Stage 2 of the pipeline: dotted-key overrides.

Overrides arrive as a click.Context, a list of --dotted.key value CLI tokens, or a {dotted.key: value} dict. :func:parse_overrides normalizes them to a dict and :func:override applies that dict to the config.

Functions

  • parse_overrides — Normalize any override specification into a plain {dotted.key: value} dict.

  • override — Patch the config in place with dotted key/value overrides.

source parse_overrides(source: Union[click.Context, list[str], dict, None]) → dict

Normalize any override specification into a plain {dotted.key: value} dict.

This is the single place that knows the different shapes overrides can arrive in, so the rest of the code only ever deals with a dict:

  • None -> {} (no overrides);
  • a click.Context -> its extra --dotted.key value args are parsed;
  • a list[str] of those same CLI tokens -> parsed directly;
  • a dict of dotted keys to already-typed values -> returned as-is.

Only the CLI forms are literal-parsed; mapping values are used verbatim, so callers passing a dict provide real Python objects (SNR=500, not "500").

Parameters

  • source : click.Context or list of str or dict or None — The override specification in any supported shape.

Returns

  • dict — Mapping of dotted key (e.g. "forward_model.instrument.SNR") to value.

source override(box: dict, ctx: Union[click.Context, list[str], dict, None]) → dict

Patch the config in place with dotted key/value overrides.

The overrides may be given in any shape accepted by :func:parse_overrides (click.Context, CLI arg list, or dict); normalization is delegated there, so this function only applies an already-canonical mapping. Keys are dotted (see :func:~.common.set_dotted), so "forward_model.instrument.SNR" resolves into nested sections, creating any that are missing.

A mapping overriding an existing section is deep-merged into it, keeping the section's other keys; any other value, including lists and None, replaces the existing one outright.

Parameters

  • box : dict — The loaded config to override; mutated in place.

  • ctx : click.Context or list of str or dict or None — The overrides, in any shape accepted by :func:parse_overrides.

Returns

  • dict — The same box, updated with the overrides.

source module isofit.configs.utils.interpolate.resolve

Stage 3 of the pipeline: ${...} reference interpolation.

:func:interpolate walks the config tree and hands each string to :func:interp, which substitutes ${key} (absolute) and ${.key} (relative) references.

Functions

  • interp — Interpolate ${...} references in a single string against the config.

  • interpolate — Recursively interpolate every ${...} reference in a config tree in place.

source interp(val: str, rel: dict, full: dict, _seen: Optional[set] = None) → Any

Interpolate ${...} references in a single string against the config.

Format: ${.key} or ${key}. A leading dot makes the key relative to the subsection the original value lives in (rel); otherwise it resolves from the top of the config (full). After substitution the result is parsed as a Python literal when possible, so a fully-substituted string can become e.g. an int/list.

Referenced values are resolved depth-first in their own context before being substituted: a referenced string has its relative refs resolved against its own section, and a referenced list or mapping is fully interpolated. Either way the resolved value is written back into the config, so each value is resolved once and the result does not depend on key order.

Parameters

  • val : str — The value to interpolate.

  • rel : dict — The subsection used to resolve relative (${.key}) references.

  • full : dict — The full config used to resolve absolute (${key}) references.

  • _seen : set, optional — Internal set of the values currently being resolved on this recursion chain, used to detect circular references. Should not be passed by callers.

Returns

  • Any — The interpolated value; a literal (int/list/...) when it parses as one, otherwise the substituted string (or val unchanged if it had no refs).

Raises

  • ValueError

  • KeyError

source interpolate(box: Union[dict, list], full: Optional[dict] = None, rel: Optional[dict] = None, _seen: Optional[set] = None) → Union[dict, list]

Recursively interpolate every ${...} reference in a config tree in place.

Walks box (a dict or list), replacing each string value via :func:interp. full is the full config used for absolute references; rel is the current subsection used for relative ones. Both default to box itself on the first call and are threaded down as the walk descends into subsections.

:func:interp resolves each referenced value depth-first and writes it back, so the result is the same whatever order the keys are walked in.

Parameters

  • box : dict or list — The config node to interpolate; mutated in place.

  • full : dict, optional — Full config for absolute references. Defaults to box on the first call.

  • rel : dict, optional — Subsection for relative references. Defaults to full.

  • _seen : set, optional — Internal set of the values currently being resolved, used by :func:interp to detect circular references. Should not be passed by callers.

Returns

  • dict or list — The same box, with all ${...} references interpolated.

source module isofit.configs.utils.accessors

Element-accessor helpers for config sections.

The pre-Pydantic BaseConfigSection exposed a handful of helper methods for iterating over the "element" fields of a config section (state-vector elements, input files, ...). A large amount of runtime code in core/, inversion/ and atmosphere/ still relies on those helpers, so this mixin restores them for the Pydantic models.

The semantics intentionally match the old base class:

  • get_all_element_names / get_all_elements return every field, in declaration order, without filtering.
  • get_elements drops fields whose value is None and returns the remaining (elements, names) sorted alphabetically by name.
  • get looks an element up by name, returning [] when absent (mirroring the historical behaviour that callers depend on).

  • StateVectorValueMixin — Per-attribute accessors for a state vector's StateVectorElementConfigs.

source module isofit.configs.base

Shared base model for config sections.

The section models carry no Python-side defaults; those live in the base configs under isofit/configs/templates/. :class:SectionModel lets a section be constructed on its own by seeding it from one of those base configs via the base keyword, e.g. ImplementationConfig(base="vswir", n_cores=4).

source class SectionModel(**data: Any)

Bases : BaseModel

Base model for config sections that can be seeded from a base config.

Passing base=<name> loads the base config name (see :func:isofit.configs.loader.load), deep-merges the remaining keyword arguments onto this model's subsection of it, interpolates ${...} references against the full config, and validates the result. base itself is not stored on the model.

Subclasses opt in by setting :attr:section to their dotted path within the full config. Without base, validation is unchanged.

Main ISOFIT configuration model.

This Pydantic model validates and manages all ISOFIT configuration parameters, including input/output files, forward model components (surface, atmosphere, instrument), and implementation settings.

from isofit.configs import Config

config.forward_model.atmosphere.engine.name

config = Config(
    base="vswir",
    forward_model={"surface": {"surface_file": "surface.mat"}},

source module isofit.configs.legacy

Upgrades configuration dicts written for older versions of ISOFIT.

The config models in :mod:isofit.configs.sections only accept the current schema. Configs written for older versions of ISOFIT are converted here first, before they are overlaid onto a base config and validated (see :func:isofit.configs.loader.load). Keeping every legacy fix in this module keeps the models free of backwards-compatibility aliases.

The legacy layouts handled are:

  • forward_model.radiative_transfer, holding the engine settings under radiative_transfer_engines alongside the statevector, lut_grid, and unknowns::
forward_model:
  radiative_transfer:
    radiative_transfer_engines:
      vswir:
        engine_name: modtran
        lut_path: ...
    statevector: {...}
  • forward_model.atmosphere with engine and atmosphere settings mixed together, either flat at the atmosphere level or all nested under engine (as written by older versions of apply_oe)::
forward_model:
  atmosphere:
    engine:
      engine_name: sRTMnet
      engine_base_dir: ...
      lut_path: ...

Both are converted to the current layout, where engine holds only the fields of the selected engine's model::

forward_model:
  atmosphere:
    engine:
      name: srtmnet
      sixs_dir: ...
    lut_path: ...

Renamed keys are also updated (e.g. engine_name -> name, lut_names -> lut_subset). Configs already in the current schema pass through unchanged.

Functions

  • engine_fields — Map each engine name to the set of fields its config model accepts.

  • engine_name — Convert an engine name, possibly a legacy one, to its current name.

  • rename — Rename legacy keys of a dict.

  • convert_radiative_transfer — Convert a legacy forward_model.radiative_transfer section to a (still possibly legacy) forward_model.atmosphere section.

  • convert_atmosphere — Split a forward_model.atmosphere section into atmosphere and engine fields, renaming legacy keys.

  • convert — Convert a config dict written for an older version of ISOFIT to the current schema.

source module isofit.configs.loader

Configuration loader utilities.

Configs are loaded either from a file on disk or from one of the base configs shipped under isofit/configs/templates/. Base configs are referenced by the name of a top-level section in one of those files (e.g. "default", "vswir", "modtran"); see :func:list_bases for the full index.

Loading resolves ^^ inheritance via :mod:isofit.configs.utils.interpolate, upgrades the result from any legacy schema via :func:isofit.configs.legacy.convert, then applies overrides and optionally ${...} interpolation. The ISOFIT environment (:data:isofit.data.env) is exposed under the env key during interpolation so configs may reference e.g. ${env.srtmnet}.

Functions

  • list_bases — Index the base configs available in :data:ConfigsDir.

  • load — Load a config dict from a file or a named base config.

  • create_new_config — Load a config and validate it into a :class:~isofit.configs.Config.

  • expand_paths — Expand relative paths in a config tree against root, in place.

source list_bases() → dict[str, Path]

Index the base configs available in :data:ConfigsDir.

Every top-level section of every template file is a base config. Files are scanned in sorted order, so if two files define the same section the first one found wins. The index is computed once and cached; the returned dict is shared, so do not mutate it.

Returns

  • dict[str, pathlib.Path] — Mapping of base config name to the template file that defines it.

Examples 

from isofit.configs.loader import list_bases
index = list_bases()
index["vswir"].name

'vswir.yml'

source load(key: Union[str, Path], section: Optional[str] = None, overrides: Optional[dict] = None, interp: bool = False) → dict

Load a config dict from a file or a named base config.

The file (or, for a base config, its section) is read with :func:isofit.configs.utils.interpolate.load (resolving ^^ inheritance, without interpolation) and upgraded from any legacy schema via :func:isofit.configs.legacy.convert; for base configs that result is stored in :data:Cache under (file, base name), while files given by path are re-read on every call. A copy of it then has overrides applied to section, and if interp is set its ${...} references are resolved against the full config, so a section may reference values outside itself (e.g. ${output.dir} from within forward_model). During interpolation the ISOFIT environment is temporarily exposed under env so configs may reference e.g. ${env.srtmnet}. Only section is returned.

Parameters

  • key : str or pathlib.Path — Either a path to a config file (.yml, .yaml, or .json) or the name of a base config (see :func:list_bases). An existing file takes precedence over a base config of the same name.

  • section : str, optional — Dotted path of the subsection to return, e.g. "forward_model.surface" (see :func:isofit.configs.utils.interpolate.get_dotted). None or "" returns the full config.

  • overrides : dict, optional — Dotted-key overrides, {"dotted.key": value}, relative to section rather than the full config. A mapping is deep-merged into an existing mapping; any other value replaces the existing one outright (see :func:isofit.configs.utils.interpolate.override).

  • interp : bool, default=False — Resolve ${...} references before returning.

Returns

  • dict — The loaded config, or its section, in the current schema.

Raises

  • ValueError — If key is neither an existing file nor a known base config.

  • KeyError — If section is not in the loaded config, or a ${...} reference cannot be resolved.

Examples 

from isofit.configs.loader import load
config = load("vswir", interp=True)
impl = load("vswir", section="implementation", overrides={"n_cores": 4})
impl["n_cores"]

4

source create_new_config(file: Union[str, Path], **kwargs) → Config

Load a config and validate it into a :class:~isofit.configs.Config.

Legacy loading function, to be deprecated in the config refactor part 2.

When file is a path, relative paths in the config (values of keys containing file, directory, or path) are expanded against the config file's directory, not the current working directory. Values that are ${...} references are left for interpolation.

Parameters

  • file : str or pathlib.Path — Path to a config file or the name of a base config; see :func:load.

  • **kwargs — Passed through to :func:load (section, overrides, interp).

Returns

  • Config — The validated config.

Raises

  • ValueError — If file is neither an existing file nor a known base config.

  • pydantic.ValidationError — If the loaded config fails validation.

Examples 

from isofit.configs import create_new_config
config = create_new_config("config.yaml")

source expand_paths(data: Union[dict, list], root: Path) → None

Expand relative paths in a config tree against root, in place.

Applies to string values of keys containing file, directory, or path. Absolute paths and values starting with a ${...} reference are left unchanged.

Parameters

  • data : dict or list — The config node to expand; mutated in place.

  • root : pathlib.Path — Directory relative paths are expanded against.

source module isofit.core.forward

Classes

  • ForwardModel — ForwardModel contains all the information about how to calculate radiance measurements at a specific spectral calibration, given a state vector. It also manages the distributions of unretrieved, unknown parameters of the state vector (i.e. the S_b and K_b matrices of Rodgers et al.

source class ForwardModel(full_config: Config, cache_atmosphere: Atmosphere = False)

ForwardModel contains all the information about how to calculate radiance measurements at a specific spectral calibration, given a state vector. It also manages the distributions of unretrieved, unknown parameters of the state vector (i.e. the S_b and K_b matrices of Rodgers et al.

State vector elements always go in the following order

(1) Surface parameters (2) Atmospheric Radiative Transfer parameters (3) Instrument parameters

Attributes

  • nbvec — Set up state vector indices - MUST MATCH ORDER FROM ABOVE ASSIGNMENT

Methods

  • clip_bounds — Clip state vector against bounds. eps shifts bounds by epsilon to not pin boundary returned val at boundary. Used when clipping prior mean. Use a relative espilon to scale with statevecor value.

  • out_of_bounds — Check if state vector is within bounds.

  • heuristic_prior_update — Get the pixel-specific priors NOTE: This has been developed with diagonal priors in mind only. If updates to off-diagonals become necessary, we would have to revisit all implementations, particularly the indexing in the PriorUpdate tuple. This is potentially a hassle with the Sa normalization

  • xa_heuristic

  • xa_static — Calculate the prior mean of the state vector (the concatenation of state vectors for the surface, atmosphere, and instrument).

  • Sa_heuristic

  • Sa_static — Calculate the prior covariance of the state vector (the concatenation of state vectors for the surface and the atmosphere).

  • Sb — Accumulate the uncertainty due to unmodeled variables within respective forward model portions.

  • eof_offset — Empirical orthogonal function offset. FM wrapper in the style of xa, Sa, Seps in case we want to be able to extend this across surface, atmosphere, and instrument

  • calc_meas — Calculate the model observation at instrument wavelengths.

  • calc_atmosphere_quantities — Retrieves the atmosphere quantities including the LUT sample (r), and the radiances (L). This function handles the hand-off between the 1c and 6c model.

  • get_L_coupled — Get the interpolated radiance terms on the sun-to-surface-to-sensor path. These follow the physics as presented in Guanter (2006), Vermote et al. (1997), and Tanre et al. (1983).

  • calc_rdn — Physics-based forward model to calculate at-sensor radiance. Includes topography, background reflectance, and glint.

  • calc_rdn_bgrfl_heterogeneous — TOA radiance that is a function of the heterogeneous background reflectance (used in AOE).

  • calc_rdn_bgrfl_homogeneous — TOA radiance that is a function of the background reflectance in homogenous case (used in AOE).

  • terrain_rereflection_heterogeneous — Isotropic scattering from nearby terrain.

  • terrain_rereflection_homogeneous — Terrain scattering is ignored in the case dir_dir=dir_dif=dif_dir=dif_dif.

  • calc_Ls — Calculate the surface emission.

  • calc_rfl — Calculate the surface reflectance.

  • calc_lamb — Calculate the Lambertian surface reflectance.

  • Seps — Calculate the total uncertainty of the observation, including up to three terms: (1) the instrument noise; (2) the uncertainty due to explicit unmodeled variables, i.e. the S_epsilon matrix of Rodgers et al.; and (3) an aggregate 'model discrepancy' term, Gamma.

  • K — Derivative of observation with respect to state vector. This is the concatenation of jacobians with respect to parameters of the surface and the atmosphere.

  • Kb — Derivative of measurement with respect to unmodeled & unretrieved unknown variables, e.g. S_b. This is the concatenation of Jacobians with respect to parameters of the surface, atmosphere, and instrument. Currently, we only treat uncertainties in the instrument and atmosphere model.

  • dmeas_datmosphere — Derivative of estimated radiance w.r.t. atmosphere statevector elements. We use a numerical approach to approximate datmosphere with a constant surface reflectance. This is a reasonable approx. for the multicomponent surface.

  • dmeas_datmosphereb — Derivative of estimated rdn w.r.t. H2O_ABSCO

  • summarize — State vector summary.

  • calibration — Calculate measured wavelengths and fwhm.

  • upsample — Linear interpolation to atmosphere wavelengths.

  • unpack — Unpack the state vector in appropriate index ordering.

  • replace_rfl

  • match_statevector

source method ForwardModel.calc_atmosphere_quantities(x_atmosphere: np.ndarray, geom: Geometry, rho_dif_dif: np.ndarray = 0)

Retrieves the atmosphere quantities including the LUT sample (r), and the radiances (L). This function handles the hand-off between the 1c and 6c model.

In the 1c case, L_dir_dir, L_dif_dir, L_dir_dif, L_dif_dif = 0, and L_tot, L_down_dir, and L_down_dif are populated within the if statement.

In the 6c case, we always use returns from get_L_coupled All quantities are on the sun-to-surface-to-sensor path.

Parameters

  • x_atmosphere : np.ndarray — atmosphere portion of the state vector.

  • geom : Geometry — Geometry object for the current observation.

  • rho_dif_dif : np.ndarray — Apparent surface reflectance for hemispherical-hemispherical photon paths. Included here to incorporate surface-atm coupling following Eq. 11 of Guanter et al., 2009.

Returns

  • r — LUT sample dictionary of shared atmosphere quantities. L_tot: total downwelling radiance (uW/nm/sr/cm2). L_dir_dir: direct-to-direct radiance component; zero in 1c mode. L_dif_dir: diffuse-to-direct radiance component; zero in 1c mode. L_dir_dif: direct-to-diffuse radiance component; zero in 1c mode. L_dif_dif: diffuse-to-diffuse radiance component; zero in 1c mode.

source method ForwardModel.get_L_coupled(r: dict, geom: Geometry, rho_dif_dif: np.ndarray = 0)

Get the interpolated radiance terms on the sun-to-surface-to-sensor path. These follow the physics as presented in Guanter (2006), Vermote et al. (1997), and Tanre et al. (1983).

Note: This function is only applicable to the 6c run case where r contains populated separated transmittances

Parameters

  • r : dict — interpolated radiative transfer quantities from the LUT

  • coszen — top-of-atmosphere solar zenith angle

  • cos_i — local solar zenith angle at the surface

Returns

  • interpolated radiances along all optical paths —

    L_dir_dir => downward direct * upward direct L_dif_dir => downward diffuse * upward direct L_dir_dif => downward direct * upward diffuse L_dif_dif => downward diffuse * upward diffuse

source modtran_rdn_in_nm(rdn, wvn)

Convert irradiance wavenumber to wavelength. Steps:

1. Wavelength (λ) and wavenumber (v) are related by λ = 1/v.
    To get λ in nanometers, use λ_nm = 10^7 / v.
2. Differential relation: dλ = -1/v^2 dv. In nanometers: dλ_nm = -10^7 / v^2 dv.
3. Conversion Formula: I_λ = I_v * |dv/dλ_nm|.
    Since dλ_nm/dv = -10^7 / v^2, the conversion factor is |dv/dλ_nm| = v^2 / 10^7.
4. Apply conversion for each wavenumber (v) to obtain irradiance in W cm^-2 / nm.
    I_λ_nm = I_v_cm^-1 * (v^2 / 10^7)
Note: This formula considers the squared relationship between v and λ and unit conversion from cm to nm.

Parameters

  • rdn : float — Irradiance in W cm^-2 / cm^-1.

  • wvn : float — Wavenumber in cm^-1.

Returns

If string, checks if this exists as a file and loads that in as the data dict replace : "dirs" | "keys" | None, default="dirs" Defines what kind of values from the ini to replace in strings: - "dirs" only replace directory paths - "keys" only replace key strings - None replaces both Recommended to only use "dirs" to remain consistent. "keys" can have unintended consequences and may replace more than it should save : bool, default=True If the data was a file and this is enabled, saves the converted data dict to another file. The new file will simply append ".tmpl" to its name report : bool, default=True Reports if no value in the input data was changed **kwargs : dict Additional strings to replace. The values are replaced in a string with the key of the kwarg. For example: 

kwargs = {"xyz": "abc"}
data["some_key"] = "replace abc here"


will be replaced as:

data["some_key"] = "replace {xyz} here"

This is to be used with Ini.fromTemplate to replace values that are not
found in the ini object

Returns

data : dict | pathlib.Path In-place replaced string values with template values If saved as a new file, returns the path instead

Raises

  • FileNotFoundError

source method Ini.fromTemplate(data: str | dict, save: bool = True, prepend: str = None, **kwargs) → dict

Recursively replaces the template values in found in string values with the real value from the ini. Template values are in the form of "{env.[value]}". This is an in-place operation.

Parameters

data : str | dict The dictionary to walk over and update values. If string, checks if this exists as a file and loads that in as the data dict save : bool, default=True If the data was a file and this is enabled, saves the converted data dict to another file. If the input file ends with ".tmpl" then it will simply be cut. If it doesn't or already exists, then the output filename will be the input filename prepended with prepend value. prepend : str, default=None Prepend a string to the output filename. If not set and the input filename doesn't end with ".tmpl", then this is auto-set to "replaced" **kwargs : dict Additional strings to replace. The values are replaced in a string with the key of the kwarg. For example: 

kwargs = {"xyz": "abc"}
data["some_key"] = "replace {xyz} here"


will be replaced as:

data["some_key"] = "replace abc here"

This is to be used with Ini.toTemplate to replace values that are not found
in the ini object

Returns

data : dict | pathlib.Path In-place replaced template values with actual from a loaded ini If saved as a new file, returns the path instead

Raises

  • FileNotFoundError

source method Ini.toTemplate(data: str | dict, replace='dirs', save: bool = True, report: bool = True, **kwargs) → dict

Recursively converts string values in a dict to be template values which can be converted back using Ini.fromTemplate(). Template values are in the form of "{env.[value]}".

Parameters

data : str | dict The dictionary to walk over and update values. If string, checks if this exists as a file and loads that in as the data dict replace : "dirs" | "keys" | None, default="dirs" Defines what kind of values from the ini to replace in strings: - "dirs" only replace directory paths - "keys" only replace key strings - None replaces both Recommended to only use "dirs" to remain consistent. "keys" can have unintended consequences and may replace more than it should save : bool, default=True If the data was a file and this is enabled, saves the converted data dict to another file. The new file will simply append ".tmpl" to its name report : bool, default=True Reports if no value in the input data was changed **kwargs : dict Additional strings to replace. The values are replaced in a string with the key of the kwarg. For example: 

kwargs = {"xyz": "abc"}
data["some_key"] = "replace abc here"


will be replaced as:

data["some_key"] = "replace {xyz} here"

This is to be used with Ini.fromTemplate to replace values that are not
found in the ini object

Returns

data : dict | pathlib.Path In-place replaced string values with template values If saved as a new file, returns the path instead

Raises

  • FileNotFoundError

source method Ini.fromTemplate(data: str | dict, save: bool = True, prepend: str = None, **kwargs) → dict

Recursively replaces the template values in found in string values with the real value from the ini. Template values are in the form of "{env.[value]}". This is an in-place operation.

Parameters

data : str | dict The dictionary to walk over and update values. If string, checks if this exists as a file and loads that in as the data dict save : bool, default=True If the data was a file and this is enabled, saves the converted data dict to another file. If the input file ends with ".tmpl" then it will simply be cut. If it doesn't or already exists, then the output filename will be the input filename prepended with prepend value. prepend : str, default=None Prepend a string to the output filename. If not set and the input filename doesn't end with ".tmpl", then this is auto-set to "replaced" **kwargs : dict Additional strings to replace. The values are replaced in a string with the key of the kwarg. For example: 

kwargs = {"xyz": "abc"}
data["some_key"] = "replace {xyz} here"


will be replaced as:

data["some_key"] = "replace abc here"

This is to be used with Ini.toTemplate to replace values that are not found
in the ini object

Returns

data : dict | pathlib.Path In-place replaced template values with actual from a loaded ini If saved as a new file, returns the path instead

Raises

  • FileNotFoundError

source class ResourceTracker(callback: Callable[[dict], None], interval: float = 2, units: tuple = ('GB', 1024 ** 3), cores: Union[int, Literal['all']] = None, round: Union[bool, int] = 2, summarize: bool = True, allow_unsafe: bool = False)

Tracks system resources

Parameters

  • callback : Callable[[dict], None] — Function to call on each resource refresh. Signature must accept:

    callable(dict) -> None

the first call will contain the non-changing values:
    used_cores : int
        Number of CPU cores in use. See the 'cores' parameter for more
    total_cores : int
        Total number of cores available on the system via os.cpu_count()
    sys_mem_total : float
        Total memory of the system
    mem_unit : str
        Unit label that the memory values are in
    mem_value : float
        The value used to convert the bytes to the mem_unit. This may be
        used to reverse the conversion
    poll_interval : float
        Resource polling interval
    timestamp : float
        The start timestamp of the resource tracker via time.time()

all calls afterwards will consist of:
    pid : int
        Main process ID
    name : str
        Main process name
    mem : float
        Main process memory used
    mem_total : float
        Approximate total memory of the process (actual + shared)
    mem_actual : float
        Approximate private memory in use by the process
    mem_shared : float
        Approximate shared memory
    cpu : float
        Main process CPU percentage over the interval
    sys_cpu_per_core : list[float]
        Per-core usage percentage over the interval
    timestamp : float
        Timestamp of the resource record via time.time()
    status : str
        Main process status, eg. 'running', 'sleeping'
    children : list[dict]
        Information of child processes:
            pid : int
                Child process ID
            name : str
                Child process name
            mem_total : float
                Approximate total memory of the child process (actual + shared)
            mem_actual : float
                Approximate private memory in use by the child process
            mem_shared : float
                Approximate shared memory
            cpu : float
                Child process CPU percentage over the interval
            status : str
                Child process status, eg. 'running', 'sleeping'

if summarize is enabled, these will also be included:
    mem_app_total : float
        Approximate total memory of the main process + children
    mem_app_actual : float
        Approximate total private memory over all processes
    mem_app_shared_avg : float
        Approximate average shared memory over all processes
    mem_used : float
        Memory in use by the system
    mem_avail : float
        Remaining available memory, defined as free + reclaimable
    cpu_avg : float
        Average CPU percentage calculated as: sum(main + children) / cores
    sys_cpu : float
        System-wide CPU percentage over the interval

  • interval : int | float, default=2 — Interval frequency in seconds to check resources Must be greater than 0. Values less than 0.1 risk high CPU usage and skewing polled results The CPU usage is calculated as the percentage of CPU used over this interval

  • units : tuple[str, float], default=("GB", 10243) — Units to convert the memory values to. Must be in the form of (str, float) where the float is used to divide the bytes values that psutil returns Some possible conversions: - ('b', 1/8) # Convert to bits (multiply by 8) - ('B', 1) # No conversion, leave as the default bytes - ('KB', 1024) # Kilobytes - ('MB', 10242) # Megabytes - ('GB', 1024**3) # Gigabytes, default

  • cores : int | 'all', default=1 — Number of cores being used by the source program. This is used for calculating the average CPU percentage. Can be passed 'all' to retrieve the os.cpu_count()

  • round : int | bool, default=2 — Round the memory variables to this many decimals. Set to False or 0 to disable True will be set to 1

  • summarize : bool, default=True — Includes summary statistics such as the sum of all children

  • allow_unsafe : bool, default=False — Bypasses the exception and allows unsafe interval values (less than 0.1) Not recommended

    • Examples

    Basic usage::

    import time
from isofit.debug.resource_tracker import ResourceTracker

def myFunction(info: dict):
    print(info)

rt = ResourceTracker(myFunction)
rt.start()
time.sleep(10)
rt.stop()

Initialization specifies retrieval subwindows for calculating measurement cost distributions.

Methods

  • full_statevector

  • calc_conditional_prior — Calculate prior distribution of radiance. This depends on the location in the state space. Return the inverse covariance and its square root (for non-quadratic error residual calculation).

  • calc_prior — Calculate prior distribution of radiance. This depends on the location in the state space. Return the inverse covariance and its square root (for non-quadratic error residual calculation).

  • calc_posterior — Calculate posterior distribution of state vector. This depends both on the location in the state space and the radiance (via noise).

  • calc_Seps — Calculate (zero-mean) measurement distribution in radiance terms. This depends on the location in the state space. This distribution is calculated over one or more subwindows of the spectrum. Return the inverse covariance and its square root.

  • jacobian — Calculate measurement Jacobian and prior Jacobians with respect to cost function. This is the derivative of cost with respect to the state, commonly known as the gradient or loss surface. The cost is expressed as a vector of 'residuals' with respect to the prior and measurement, expressed in absolute (not quadratic) terms for the solver; It is the square root of the Rodgers (2000) Chi-square version. All measurement distributions are calculated over subwindows of the full spectrum. Args: x_free: decision variables - portion of the statevector not fixed by a static integration grid geom: Geometry to use for inversion Seps_inv_sqrt: Inverse square root of the covariance of "observation noise", including both measurement noise from the instrument as well as variability due to unknown variables.

  • loss_function — Calculate cost function expressed here in absolute (not quadratic) terms for the solver, i.e., the square root of the Rodgers (2000) Chi-square version. We concatenate 'residuals' due to measurment and prior terms, suitably scaled. All measurement distributions are calculated over subwindows of the full spectrum.

  • invert — Inverts a meaurement and returns a state vector. Args: meas: a one-D scipy vector of radiance in uW/nm/sr/cm2 geom: a geometry object

  • forward_uncertainty — Can this be depreciated? Uncertainty file is generated by a direct call to calc_posterior.

source module isofit.inversion.inverse_simple

Functions

  • heuristic_atmosphere — From a given radiance, estimate atmospheric state with band ratios. Used to initialize gradient descent inversions.

  • invert_algebraic — Inverts radiance algebraically using Lambertian assumptions to get a reflectance. If the appropriate transmittance terms are available, surface slope will enter for the initial guess. Otherwise, the surface will be treated as if flat.

  • invert_analytical — Perform an analytical estimate of the conditional MAP estimate for a fixed atmosphere. Based on the "Inner loop" from Susiluoto et al. (2025). doi: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs17223719

  • invert_simple — Find an initial guess at the state vector. This currently uses traditional (non-iterative, heuristic) atmospheric correction.

  • invert_liquid_water — Given a reflectance estimate, fit a state vector including liquid water path length based on a simple Beer-Lambert surface model.

  • beer_lambert_model — Function, which computes the vector of residuals between measured and modeled surface reflectance optimizing for path length of surface liquid water based on the Beer-Lambert attenuation law.

source calc_shards(grid, wl, chunk, storage='8gb', target_shards=None, scale=1)

Determine an optimal Zarr sharding strategy for a LUT and group points by shard.

This function computes candidate shard shapes that: - evenly divide the LUT dimensions - do not split chunks - approximately match a target storage size per shard

It then selects the shard shape whose number of chunks per shard is closest to the target, and groups LUT points into shard-aligned partitions.

Parameters

  • grid : dict[str, Iterable] — LUT grid definition as {dimension_name: values}. These define the non-wavelength dimensions of the LUT.

  • wl : iterable — Wavelength dimension values.

  • chunk : iterable of int — Chunk shape used for Zarr storage. Must align with the full LUT shape (wl + grid dimensions).

  • storage : str or float, default="8gb" — Storage size limit per shard. Determines how many chunks should be grouped into a shard while respecting the limit.

  • target_shards : int, optional — Target number of shards to produce. The closest sharding strategy to this will be selected.

  • scale : int, default=1 — Multiplier applied to the estimated chunk size. Useful when multiple arrays are written per chunk to better approximate the actual memory when in buffered mode.

Returns

  • best : np.array[int] — Selected shard shape, including the wavelength dimension as the first axis.

  • groups : dict[tuple[int, ...], list[tuple]] — Mapping from shard index (multi-dimensional shard ID) to the list of grid points (coordinate tuples) that fall within that shard.

  • coords : dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[slice, ...]] — Mapping from shard index to the corresponding global array slice (including wavelength as the leading dimension). These slices can be used directly to write shard-aligned data into a Zarr array.

Raises

  • ValueError

source shardWriter(lut, shard, coord, points, simmer, reader)

Execute simulations for a set of points and write chunked results to a LUT shard.

This function is intended to run as a Ray remote task. For each input point, it runs a simulation, reads the resulting data, separates chunked and non-chunked outputs, and queues the chunked data into a shard buffer. After all points are processed, the buffered data is flushed to disk.

Parameters

  • lut : dict or LUT-like — Either a dictionary of arguments used to initialize a LUT via luts.create or an already-instantiated LUT Create object.

  • shard : int or str — Identifier for the shard being processed. Used for logging.

  • coord : tuple of slice or similar — Coordinate slices defining the region of the LUT corresponding to this shard.

  • points : iterable — Collection of input points to simulate and process. These points are assumed to be in the same shard.

  • simmer : callable — Function to run the simulation.

  • reader : callable — Function to read the results of the simulation.

Returns

  • tuple — A tuple (point, chunkless) where point is the last processed point and chunkless is a dictionary of non-chunked outputs from the last iteration.

source package isofit.surface

Classes

  • GlintModelSurface — A model of the surface based on a collection of multivariate Gaussians, extended with two surface glint terms (sun + sky glint).

  • LUTSurface — A model of the surface based on an N-dimensional lookup table indexed by one or more state vector elements. We calculate the reflectance by multilinear interpolation. This is good for surfaces like aquatic ecosystems or snow that can be described with just a few degrees of freedom.

  • MultiComponentSurface — A model of the surface based on a collection of multivariate Gaussians, with one or more equiprobable components and full covariance matrices.

source class GlintModelSurface(full_config: Config)

Bases : MultiComponentSurface

A model of the surface based on a collection of multivariate Gaussians, extended with two surface glint terms (sun + sky glint).

Methods

  • heuristic_prior_update — Get the updates for xa, Sa, Sa_inv, Sa_inv_sqrt. The format follows: xa: (statevec_idx: list[int], update_values: ndarray[float]) Sa: (statevec_idx: list[int], update_values: ndarray[float]) Sa_inv: (statevec_idx: list[int], update_values: ndarray[float]) Sa_inv_sqrt: (statevec_idx: list[int], update_values: ndarray[float])

  • xa — Mean of prior distribution, calculated at state x.

  • Sa — Covariance of prior distribution, calculated at state x. We find the covariance in a normalized space (normalizing by z) and then un- normalize the result for the calling function.

  • fit_params — Given a reflectance estimate and one or more emissive parameters, fit a state vector.

  • calc_rfl — Direct and diffuse Reflectance (includes sun and sky glint).

  • drfl_dsurface — Partial derivative of reflectance with respect to state vector, calculated at x_surface.

  • drdn_dglint — Derivative of radiance with respect to the direct and diffuse glint terms

  • drdn_dsurface — Derivative of radiance with respect to full surface vector

  • analytical_model — Linearization of the glint terms to use in AOE inner loop. Function will fetch the linearization of the rho terms and add the matrix components for the direct glint term.
